elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: Inserted paragraph: "Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates..." — express defence duty running to Customer and its Affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: "...from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees)" in favour of Customer and its Affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Limb (a): "an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Limb (c): "any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Limb (d): "Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: "Customer shall give Vendor written notice of the claim".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: "Vendor shall control its defence and settlement" — control expressly allocated to Vendor.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: "Customer shall indemnify Vendor only against third-party claims arising out of content Customer provides to the Services and Customer's breach of Applicable Law" — the word "only" confines the Customer indemnity to the two permitted heads.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: Limb (a) of the inserted paragraph covers third-party allegations that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate IP rights.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: no such exclusion is inserted, and none is required of us; the condition (accepting an exclusion) does not apply, so nothing is owed.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; the redline contains no combination carve-out and none is required for the level to be reached.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no specification carve-out is inserted and none is required.

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: The inserted paragraph contains no procure/modify/replace remedy ladder; nothing in the rendered language obliges Vendor to secure continued use or to modify or replace the infringing Services or Deliverables.

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: No refund-of-fees backstop appears anywhere in the inserted indemnity or in the retained text.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No 3× annual-fees super-cap is inserted; Section 21.3 continues to treat indemnification obligations as Excluded Claims (uncapped).

reasons: Preferred level is position-complete: all ten preferred elements appear in operative language in a single inserted indemnity paragraph (defence and indemnity for Customer and Affiliates; four covered heads; notice/control/cooperation; Customer indemnity narrowed by "only").

Fallback level is incomplete (no procure/modify/replace ladder, no refund backstop, no 3× super-cap), but that is immaterial because the preferred checklist is fully met; targeting preferred is also the better outcome for us since a 3× super-cap would be worse than the existing uncapped treatment of indemnification obligations in Section 21.3.

Minimal: the insertion tracks the model language and adds nothing outside the preferred checklist — no survival tail, no extra damages categories, no settlement-consent or mitigation mechanics, and no amendment to the retained liability or warranty text.

Intent preserved: Section 19.5's reference to an "indemnity" and Section 21.3's "indemnification obligations" Excluded Claim now have a clause to attach to, and no retained sentence contradicts the insertion.

Housekeeping to fix in the operative text (not element defects): the insertion carries the heading "INDEMNIFICATION." with no section number — number it "20. INDEMNIFICATION" so the placement between Sections 19 and 21 is unambiguous, and note that Section 9.3's pre-existing cross-reference to "Section 20.5" remedies still has no corresponding subsection; either renumber that reference or, if Vendor asks, add the procure/modify/replace/refund ladder as 20.5.

Confirm that "Affiliates", "Deliverables", "Applicable Law" and "Customer Data" are defined terms in Section 1; if any is not, either define it or use lower-case descriptive wording so the insertion leaves no undefined term.
